article: sviber is a desktop-style editor for Sunniesnow charts. A chart contains timing, events,
channels, snappees, comments, media references, and editor state.
Saving a chart keeps the editable data;
exporting a level produces Sunniesnow-compatible chart data.
The web version is an installable PWA and caches its application shell and translations for
In the NW.js desktop app, File > New project... and Open project folder...
manage a folder containing project.sviber and one editable JSON file per chart.
A folder containing legacy sviber-project.json is also accepted;
and the legacy file is migrated on save. The manifest contains ordered charts
each chart keeps its own music and image reference. Only the current chart can be unsaved;
project-level changes (chart list, active chart, macros) write immediately.
The browser opens one JSON chart at a time,
disables project commands (including Open recent...), and saves by download.
Desktop sviber can also run as a CLI without the GUI using --export,
opening a supplied path starts a new instance.
New charts default to difficulty name Master with its preset color (Special with its own
preset color when Master already exists in the project), difficulty 12, offset 0,
and initial BPM 120; the charter defaults to the name last entered while creating a chart,
and opening or importing a chart does not change that default.
The difficulty color switches to a preset only when the user actually edits the difficulty
name. New project... asks whether to add a currently open standalone chart.
adds a chart to an open project and inherits the previously open chart's music and image;
outside a project it creates a standalone chart. Opening, importing,
or pasting a chart while a desktop project is open asks whether to add it to that project.
prompt to save if the current chart is unsaved. Reload chart from disk (desktop,
known path) rereads the chart file, stays in the same project,
and warns that unsaved changes will be discarded. Save
saving a new chart in a project also writes project.sviber. Save as...
chooses a new file and does not involve projects. Save project
is grayed out with no project; with a known project path it is the same as Save;
otherwise choose a directory that may contain other files but must not already contain
packages all project charts and their referenced assets,
or only the standalone chart and current media,
includes README and other display text files from the project folder,
and strips all sviber data from chart JSON. Export Lyrica chart...
(desktop) does nothing if the chosen chart or project is already open.
A chart that belongs to the current project becomes the active chart.
A chart from another project asks whether to open it in that project; if not,
and a project is already open, it asks whether to add the chart to the current project;
otherwise it opens as a standalone chart. Rename chart...
(project only) edits the filename stem with an uneditable .json suffix;
a collision is rejected, and the rename is immediate and not undoable.
If a project is open and Edit chart properties... changes the difficulty name,
it offers to rename the file to difficultyName.json when that name is free.
Delete chart... immediately writes the project JSON.
The NW.js toolbar has a chart selector while a project is open.
Each option is shown as difficulty name rating superscript;
the difficulty name uses its configured color.
Switching charts asks whether to save pending changes, immediately writes activeChart,
and loads that chart's own media. The selector is not shown in the browser,
where only one chart is open.
A new chart starts with an active rectangular Playfield grid from (-100,50)
Set music from File > Set music.... The offset is the audio time of beat zero;
the initial BPM and ordered BPM changes convert beat positions to seconds.
Beat zero can be before or after the audio beginning.
Opening a saved chart restores its saved current time, subdivision,
By default, a dirty chart is saved to the local recovery list every 120 seconds.
The interval is configurable; zero disables autosave.
Startup offers every recovery newer than the last manual save before reopening the last
document. In NW.js, restoring a recovery also restores its project and chart path context,
then reloads relative music and background references automatically.
Autosave records omit the generated top-level event list to reduce storage;
ordinary chart and project saves include it.
History entries distinguish manual saves from autosaves.
The workspace has a menu bar, toolbar, timeline, status panel, scroll view,
main editor field, side panels, history, and a tooltip bar.
The scroll view and Checks panel share the space to the left of the main field and switch
Hover near the left edge of the main editor field to reveal a DOM button that hides or
shows both the scroll view and the Checks panel.
Hover near the right edge to reveal a button that hides or shows the Inspector, Channels,
Snappees, Clips, and History panels together. Neither group is hidden by default;
hiding either group gives the main field more width. The History panel has no title.
The timeline contains a waveform, beat lines, channel lanes,
Its background is a relative note-density heat map for tap, drag, hold,
and flick events per second: the highest density is #7f1f1f and the lowest is #1f1f1f.
The yellow line is current time. Green end handles change the visible range;
the green middle bar moves both ends. The current time may be outside the visible range.
On the scrollbar, the yellow current-time line has priority over the green handles and bar;
blue A-B marks are indicators only and cannot be dragged. Hold <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Space</kbd>
while dragging to pan the visible range without changing current time, even when locked.
while clicking or dragging anywhere on the scrollbar instead sets the current time to the
pointer position snapped to subdivisions; if the visible range contained the current time,
it moves along so the current time keeps its visual position inside the range.
Clicking a lane seeks to its time and makes that lane current.
Clicking and dragging on an empty lane makes a live rectangular selection;
a three-pixel movement threshold keeps a click from becoming a drag. Holding <kbd>Alt</kbd>
and dragging anywhere in the lanes moves every selected event to the position under the
mouse (the governing event is the selected event closest to the press and lands on the
snapped beat and the lane under the pointer),
so nothing else gets selected and no duration handle can be grabbed by mistake.
Like the main field's Shift drag, this gesture has no three-pixel movement threshold.
If the pointer leaves the visible range, the range chases it;
if it leaves the shown channels, the channel list scrolls. <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>
adds to selection and <kbd>Alt</kbd> removes from selection. <kbd>Shift</kbd>
-drag selects an inclusive channel range and a time range whose end is exclusive.
Dragging an event moves it in time; dragging its white duration handle changes its end time;
holding <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd> enlarges the handle and its hit box.
Selection handles everywhere take priority over directly dragging events.
Moving selected events to the channel above or below updates tip-point connectors
The vertical channel-scroll position is saved in sviber.editor.timelineChannelOffset
and restored when the chart is loaded.
Timeline and stage drags are coalesced to animation frames;
their lightweight previews update the canvases and status only,
while panels and history are refreshed when the gesture ends.
Ordinary wheel movement seeks by one subdivision. Ctrl
keeping the current time's visual position if it is inside the range,
+wheel scrolls channel lanes even when the pointer is outside the timeline canvas,
unless the pointer is in a scrollable DOM element.
Clicking the overview track outside the green range bar pages the visible range by one
visible span toward the clicked side; if the current time is inside the old range,
it moves by the same span, otherwise it stays unchanged. <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>
-clicking or dragging anywhere on the overview track instead sets current time to the
pointer position snapped to subdivisions and, when the current time was inside the range,
moves the range to preserve its visual position. <kbd>PageUp</kbd>
shifts the range toward negative time and <kbd>PageDown</kbd> toward positive time.
When a channel is selected with <kbd>Alt</kbd>+Up/Down or <kbd>Alt</kbd>+1..9/<kbd>Alt</kbd>
+0, the lane scrollbar follows it when needed and event-creation mode stays active.
Number and Space shortcuts remain active when a status checkbox or the difficulty selector
Click or drag the waveform to seek. While dragging, time does not snap;
it snaps on mouse up if music is not playing. Snapped-time operations (adding events, BPM,
bar line, paste) are disabled while dragging. <kbd>Shift</kbd>
+drag on the waveform manages A-B marks.
Pressing away from an existing mark discards a complete pair and creates one mark at the
the second mark appears as soon as the pointer reaches another subdivision and then follows
Pressing close to an existing mark (within six pixels) moves that mark instead and keeps
the other one fixed, and the moved mark may pass it. Marks are always snapped,
the visible range chases the pointer,
and releasing on the other mark's subdivision leaves a single mark.
Beat-line positions and colors are relative to the latest bar line,
while each red line is labeled with its absolute beat number;
fractional labels use integer-plus-fraction notation and bar lines are thick red lines.
Press <kbd>R</kbd> to add or remove one at the current time;
snapping and the metronome follow these relative beats. One A-B mark is a bright blue line.
Two marks add a translucent blue interval and two blue lines even when the subdivision
differs. BPM changes are shown as purple numbers.
Seeking while stopped snaps to the nearest subdivision except when a command explicitly
The status panel has no title. It shows the time to three decimal places,
the current beat using the current subdivision denominator,
and the playback speed together on one line without labels,
wrapping to more lines when one line cannot fit them,
followed by comments active at the current time and the current operation.
If events are selected, it also shows how many. A selected comment is red here;
other comments use the normal text color. Its icon controls have no visible text labels.
Background-event icons independently hide/show bg notes, big text,
and background patterns in the timeline/scroll view or main field.
and menu/mouse-wheel seeking do not follow or resize the range. The scrollbar, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>
+wheel, and keyboard range commands remain usable.
• SE: globally enables note hit sounds, not including bg note SE.
Events in inactive channels are always silent.
• Bg note SE: enables a synthetic bg-note hit sound. Off by default.
restores the time and visible range captured when playback began.
short synthesized click whenever the time is an integer number of beats from the latest bar
line. Every click uses the same sound and level; there is no strong-beat/weak-beat accent.
Its level follows the Preferences SE volume.
• Show HUD (show-hud.svg): on by default. When checked,
the main field shows the top-left title and pause button, top-center combo,
top-right difficulty/score, and the progress bar.
• Show chart boundary: on by default. When checked,
the main field draws the chart boundary rectangle.
top and left rulers appear in the main field. The scale inside the chart bounds is white;
the scale outside is light gray; ticks and numbers are dark gray.
A very noticeable triangle marker follows the mouse.
Major and minor ticks change with main-field zoom.
• Read-only: keeps event selection, time/range navigation, Music commands,
and channel/snappee activation available while disabling other chart, snappee, channel,
history, and macro mutations. The macro window remains available;
global macros stay editable, project macros become read-only, and no macro can run.
toggles it even while a popup form is active,
and the checkbox follows fullscreen changes made by the runtime. In NW.js, <kbd>Esc</kbd>
The main field previews the chart at the current time.
Group rings around notes are larger than the note body.
Events attached to the selected snappee in an active channel also get a same-rule circle in
Background patterns and big text are not selected by clicking their preview;
select them from the timeline or Channels panel.
Click an event to select it without changing time; click a selected event again to clear it;
Selected objects remain visibly marked even when outside the current preview time.
Inactive channels and their tip points are hidden and cannot be selected.
The HUD copies Sunniesnow's layout, including the top-left title and pause button.
Clicking the pause button runs the same action as play/pause and loses to event or snappee
Manual search keeps the full manual visible and jumps to the first matching paragraph,
list item, or table row as you type. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd>
to move downward to the next match, or <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> to move upward;
Drag a movable event to change position.
A single event can attach automatically to the nearest active snap point;
attached events can be moved according to their snappee type.
Simultaneous tap pairs are connected by a double-tap line that follows their live positions
during drag previews. <kbd>Shift</kbd>-drag moves the current selection; holding <kbd>Alt</kbd>
+<kbd>Shift</kbd> is equivalent. While Shift is held,
the mouse does nothing else in the main field,
so you need not aim at a selected event or avoid other hits.
If how the events move depends on which event is being dragged,
the governing event is the closest selected event at mouse down.
If no movable event is selected, the same gesture moves the selected snappee;
any of its snap points can align to a nearby point on another active snappee. <kbd>Escape</kbd>
applies it when the inspector is not editing a field; in a matrix field,
Enter submits that element instead of confirming free transform. <kbd>Esc</kbd>
in a focused inspector field unfocuses it and restores the value.
The inspector matrix numbers update live. Translating, scaling,
or rotating past the chart boundary clamps so the would-be out-of-bound event lands exactly
Groups, clips, timing, and live hosting
creates a recursive group with a colored anchor at the selected movable events' center.
Group selection applies to descendants for movement, transforms, deletion,
an attached group can still be moved when it is the only selected root. Ungroup
restores children at the same level. Group rings appear in the timeline, main field,
and Scroll view, and a selected group has a colored bounds rectangle in all three views.
The crosshair anchor for a selected group appears only in the main editor field.
Dragging it moves the selected group anchors while leaving children in place;
anchors can snap to direct children or active snappees. Lock
protects every selected event: editing, transform,
and deletion operations ignore locked events as if they were not selected,
free transform is unavailable when the whole selection is locked,
and locked events show no flick direction handles in the main field and no duration tail
Selected locked events use a magenta tint instead of the bright red one,
and deleting a channel still removes its locked events.
its displayed time is derived from its earliest descendant.
A normal click on a grouped event selects its nearest parent group,
and clicking that selected group again clears it.
Double-click enters one group level temporarily;
nested groups are entered from the outside inward,
and the scope exits when it has no selected descendants.
Save to clips stores the relative event tree, channel attributes,
and referenced snappees in the Clips panel. Each row separates its 42px thumbnail, name,
and five actions with clear spacing. Clips can be pasted, renamed, reordered, or deleted.
Paste with options... can duplicate referenced channels and/or snappees,
including references nested in groups. The Timing
menu edits offset and initial BPM and copies or pastes the complete timing map
independently from event clipboard data. In NW.js,
over HTTP and can publish sscharter WebSocket updates;
Browser builds do not start these servers.
The scroll view is to the left of the main field and shares that space with the Checks
panel; switch them with tabs. Horizontal position is chart x;
vertical position is time, with later time higher.
The current-time line stays three quarters of the way down from the top,
exactly one quarter of the panel height from the bottom, while events move through it.
Hold and background-note durations have vertical tails. Inactive-channel events are hidden.
Background-note icons are drawn below other event icons; among other icons,
later times are drawn above earlier times.
Tip-point chains use a translucent white connector,
and a thin dark-yellow segment at the first event shows the spawn direction.
Each connector is drawn only for an adjacent pair in the same guide with at least one
visible endpoint, so unrelated off-screen notes cannot create a full-width line.
The scroll view uses the same pixels-per-second scale vertically as the timeline uses
horizontally. Its x-range is Sunniesnow's default play-field width (250).
Its visible time span can therefore extend beyond the music.
Horizontal beat lines use the timeline colors, the current time is a bright yellow line,
and red labels mark integer beats. A-B loop marks draw bright blue horizontal lines;
when both marks exist a translucent blue band covers the interval.
Group rings and selected-group bounds remain visible,
but group anchors are not drawn or hit-tested here. Click an icon to select it; <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>
adds and <kbd>Alt</kbd> removes. Drag on empty space to box-select by event centers;
the selection follows the pointer live and is committed when the drag ends.
Hold <kbd>Ctrl+Space</kbd> to pan the falling preview:
dragging downward moves toward later time, and dragging upward moves toward earlier time.
While dragging, time does not snap and snapped-time operations are disabled;
it snaps on mouse up if music is not playing.
The scroll view never edits event positions or times.
The Inspector shows common properties of the selected events and shows a gray message
when nothing is selected. Its channel dropdown lists channel names rather than numbers.
For a group it shows the read-only time derived from the earliest descendant and an
editable color, but no event type or channel field. <kbd>Esc</kbd>
in a focused inspector field unfocuses it and restores the value. Channels can be activated,
duplicated, reordered, renamed from the right-side Channels panel, edited, or deleted;
deactivating a channel deselects its events and prevents their preview and sound.
Channel and snappee items keep activation and expansion controls on their primary row;
expanding reveals an inline second row for duplicate, move up/down, rename, delete,
timeline visibility, and channel creation actions.
Clip items keep paste on the primary row and reveal their other actions the same way.
Expanded state is saved with channels, snappees, and clips.
Hiding a channel (Ctrl+J) collapses it out of the timeline lanes while its events stay
visible in the scroll view and the main editor field.
Separators over collapsed hidden channels are thick and bright gray,
turn bright yellow when the current channel is hidden,
and also appear above or below the shown lanes when hidden channels lie just outside the
Selected hidden events mark a visible separator with short red or magenta segments at their
event times. Snappees can be activated, duplicated, reordered, edited, or deleted;
deleting one detaches its events while keeping their resolved positions.
Double-clicking a row opens its edit form. The History panel has no title.
History stores up to 1000 changes and marks manual and automatic saves separately;
undo also restores the time-snapping mode, current beat/time,
and visible timeline range captured before the edit. Existing history labels,
are translated again immediately when the interface language changes.
The Checks panel shares the left space with the scroll view.
It lists live chart-check violations, untimed items first, then timed items in time order.
Its tab shows the current number of violations in red whenever it is not zero,
updated in real time. Click an item to go to the problem (an event or a properties form).
Double-click opens Edit > Checks... with that check focused.
Hover shows details in the tooltip bar. Checks...
enables or disables each check and edits its parameters;
disabled checks gray their parameter fields. All checks start enabled.
• Empty title, artist, or charter: title, artist,
and charter must be filled. Click opens Edit chart properties.
• Irregular difficulty: name must be Easy, Normal, Hard, Master,
or Special with the matching preset color. Easy–Master need a positive integer rating;
Special may be a positive integer or a single character.
A rating greater than 6 may use superscript +;
otherwise the superscript must be empty. Click opens Edit chart properties.
• Too many required fingers (default 2): canonical playability. Tap, hold,
and flick need a finger down at their time; simultaneous ones need that many fingers.
A drag needs a finger at its position but can share one with a same-position tap.
A hold keeps its finger until it ends, so a tap during a hold needs another finger,
while a drag during a hold does not. Click selects the event that needs the extra finger.
and flick must stay inside the chart boundary. Click selects the event.
• Out-of-boundary bg notes: bg notes must stay inside the chart boundary.
• Too short hold (default 0.1 s): holds must last at least that long.
big text and background patterns must last at least that long. Click selects the event.
from spawn to the last connected event. Click selects the first connected event.
• Sharp turns of tip points: a tip point must not turn by π;
consecutive events at the same time and position count as one turning point.
simultaneous events on the same tip point must share a position. Click selects those events.
• Multi-character CJK texts: if tap, hold, flick,
or bg-note text contains a CJK character, the whole text must be that single character.
“啊a” and “啊啊” fail; “啊” and “aa” pass. Click selects the event.
• Events outside music: no event may start before the music or end after it.
• Drag screening (defaults 0.4 s and 40 units): with Lyrica 5 mechanics,
a drag that has no other note near it in the screening window before its time (so it is
still unjudged) must not have a non-drag note near it in the window after its time,
or that note becomes unhittable. Click selects the drag.
and flick events (never drag) must not share a position;
positions within floating-point tolerance count as equal. With invisibleOnly
enabled, only invisible body overlaps count: same-position holds;
same-position taps when another simultaneous tap exists;
and same-position hold+tap or flick+tap where the tap is drawn behind the other note.

Run macro... asks whether to use a global or project macro,

The global/project radio is remembered until sviber exits.

The Timing menu mnemonic is Alt+T and Transform is Alt+R.
On Mac keyboards every listed Ctrl is the Command key and every Alt is the Option key,
both here and in the menus and tooltips.
Show available version, runtime, commit, and license information.
Creation tools remain active after each placement; clicking the active Tap, Hold, Drag,
Flick, or background-note tool again exits that mode.
Timeline interaction does not exit creation mode,
although events cannot be created while playback is running.
Hold and background-note duration defaults remember the last value used for that type.
Snap-to-point uses a chart-coordinate distance threshold of 6.25.
During creation and attachment, points outside the chart boundary are rejected;
only a tiny numeric tolerance is used for points that should mathematically lie exactly on
the boundary. Other in/out-of-bounds checks have no tolerance.
For an open Pen or Bézier curve, the segment count is the number of intervals,
so three segments have four snap points including both endpoints;
a closed curve has one snap point per segment.
Timeline and stage dragging use a three-pixel pointer threshold;
the Shift drags (main field) and the timeline's Alt+Shift drag are exceptions and apply to
while dragging the timeline or scroll view to pan visible time;

Channel rows provide visibility, duplicate, reorder, edit, and delete actions;

Snappee rows provide activate/deactivate, duplicate, reorder, edit, and delete actions.

A selected snappee can be translated or transformed even when no events are selected.
inherit continues the previous guide, chain starts a guide,
drop starts a one-event guide, and none stops a guide.
Spawn position can be absolute or relative; spawn time can be seconds or beats.
Inherit and none hide every tip-point field except spawn type.
Switching inherit to chain or drop fills inherited spawn params if any, otherwise defaults.
Absolute mode shows coordinates (and attachment when a snappee exists);
relative mode shows distance and direction; unused fields are hidden.

Forward playback follows the chart timing and plays music, note sounds,
the synthetic bg-note sound when Bg note SE is enabled, hit effects,
and the constant-tone metronome when enabled.
Starting at a time never replays note sounds or hit effects from before that exact time.
Hit effects disappear immediately when the music stops.
Reverse playback moves time backward, leaves music muted, and can still play note sounds,
bg note SE, and metronome clicks; it does not play hit effects.
Inactive channels never contribute to playback.
With two marks, the earlier mark is A and the later mark is B.
Forward playback returns to A at B without an audible gap;
reverse playback returns to B at A.
Boundary notes and metronome clicks are scheduled once per pass.
If a loop jump leaves the visible range,
the range moves by the minimum amount unless it is locked.
Seeking while playing pauses only for the interaction and resumes in the same direction.
Changing the visible range never interrupts playback. When playback ends or is paused,
time snaps to the nearest subdivision unless Seek back after playing is enabled,
in which case the captured time and visible range are restored. Lock visible range
prevents follow mode and menu/mouse-wheel seeking from moving the range, but not scrollbar,
and live-hosting operations report success or failure in stacked bottom-right toasts.
Live-hosting startup includes the full URL to the hosted .ssc
and the live reload port; stopping and errors are also reported.

Preferences are global and do not create chart history. They include Light, Dark,
or System theme; interface language; note speed; SE volume; music volume;
live-hosting address and reload port in NW.js; and autosave interval in seconds.
SE volume and music volume both default to 1 and use a range slider from 0 to 2 in steps of
0.05. The default autosave interval is 120 seconds, and zero disables it.
Language choices are translated into the active interface language: English,
The main editor, macro page (including the console), and manual share the saved theme.
Explicit Dark or Light always wins; System follows the operating-system color preference.
Extra undocumented functions or classes in the macro sandbox are not user-facing.
The language choice is remembered separately for the manual.

Every event record carries selected and locked booleans.
Standalone desktop charts store absolute media paths;
project charts store paths relative to the project folder.
Group records contain recursive children but no time or channel.

If audio fails, reload once and check the warning area;

If a saved chart opens with an unexpected timeline,
